- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes unrealistically; increase forecast for early days (1–3d) to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated downward moves; cap downward corrections at 50% of spike magnitude.
- Model underestimates true price drops when sentiment is negative and recent history shows mean reversion; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 1–3d if sentiment < 0.33.
- For 30d horizon, model often overestimates early days (1–7d) when sentiment is positive; apply 10–20% downward adjustment to first 5 days if sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +1.00 or -1.00 extremes, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter to reduce amplitude of extreme forecasts by 20–40%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows low volatility, model often underestimates true price; add 0.05–0.15 to forecast for 1–7d if sentiment is stable.
